::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" icon="false" title="Purpose"}
Use this guide with the Week 6 readings and class activities. Your completed
notes should help you select an appropriate hypothesis test, state formal
hypotheses, and distinguish a statistical result from its practical meaning.

Keep the finished guide as a reference for later homework, quizzes, projects,
and the practicum.
:::

## Objectives

- explain why sample estimates require an uncertainty check;
- interpret p-values, confidence intervals, and Bayes factors correctly;
- state null and alternative hypotheses in context;
- match an analytical story and its variables to an appropriate test; and
- separate statistical evidence from practical importance.

## Resources

- [Week 6 slides](week_06.qmd)
- the **Statistics Refresher** readings in Canvas
- the *Stats Jargon* excerpt provided privately in Canvas

Complete each response in your own words. Use a business example whenever the
prompt asks for an interpretation; definitions alone are not enough to show
how a concept affects a decision.
:::

## 3) Write formal hypotheses

Complete the missing alternative hypotheses. State hypotheses about population
parameters or population relationships, not about the observed sample.

| Analytical story | Null hypothesis | Alternative hypothesis |
|---|---|---|
| Difference between 2 population means | $H_0: \mu_A = \mu_B$ |  |
| Difference between 2 population medians | $H_0$: The population medians are equal. |  |
| Difference among more than 2 population means | $H_0: \mu_1 = \mu_2 = \cdots = \mu_k$ |  |
| One population mean compared with a benchmark $\mu_0$ | $H_0: \mu = \mu_0$ |  |
| Distribution compared with expected proportions | $H_0$: The population distribution matches the expected proportions. |  |
| Relationship between 2 categorical variables | $H_0$: The variables are independent in the population. |  |
| Linear relationship between 2 quantitative variables | $H_0: \rho = 0$ |  |
| Linear change in an outcome as a predictor changes | $H_0: \beta_1 = 0$ |  |

## 5) Match the story to a test

Complete the test and evidence columns as each method is introduced in class.

| Analytical story | Variables and design | Useful estimate or plot | Appropriate test | Evidence reported |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Compare means for 2 independent groups | 1 quantitative outcome; 1 categorical grouping variable with 2 independent groups | Group means and confidence intervals |  |  |
| Compare means for paired observations | 1 quantitative outcome measured twice or in matched pairs | Mean paired difference and confidence interval |  |  |
| Compare medians for 2 independent groups | Quantitative or ordinal outcome with 2 independent groups; mean is inappropriate | Group medians and boxplots |  |  |
| Compare medians for paired observations | Quantitative or ordinal outcome measured twice or in matched pairs | Median paired difference |  |  |
| Compare means across more than 2 groups | 1 quantitative outcome; 1 categorical grouping variable with more than 2 groups | Group means and confidence intervals |  |  |
| Compare one mean with a benchmark | 1 quantitative variable and a meaningful benchmark | Sample mean and confidence interval |  |  |
| Compare observed and expected category distributions | 1 categorical variable and expected proportions | Observed and expected counts or percentages |  |  |
| Examine a relationship between categorical variables | 2 categorical variables | Cross-tabulation and clustered or stacked bar chart |  |  |
| Examine a linear relationship | 2 quantitative variables | Correlation and scatterplot |  |  |
| Estimate change in an outcome | Quantitative outcome and quantitative predictor | Scatterplot with fitted line and slope |  |  |
